title: CloudFront and Global Accelerator
scenario: Nightjar Studios ships a multiplayer game whose launcher downloads 4 GB patch files from a single storage origin in one Region; about 30,000 players fetch each new patch in release week, from 40 countries, and finance wants origin data transfer and origin load cut sharply. The launcher's account API shares the website hostname under /api/, returns per-player JSON and must never serve one player another player's response. The matchmaking servers speak a custom UDP protocol to game clients; tournament partners allow-list only a fixed, published set of IP addresses, and the session endpoint must fail over between two Regions within 60 seconds of one becoming unhealthy.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
The launcher uses one hostname for patches and the API, and that hostname cannot change
When a new patch is published, the origin may serve it to the delivery network only a few times, not once for each location that players connect from
Tournament partners will accept only a fixed set of published addresses, and it must not change when traffic fails over between Regions
requiredArtifact: Architecture decision record + diagram notes + cost assumptions

rubric.label: Why live lab was unsuitable documented

Patch downloads are served from close to the players, per-player API responses are never shared between players, both on the single hostname, and a new 4 GB patch is pulled from the origin only a few times regardless of how many locations players connect from
UDP game sessions reach a fixed, allow-listable set of addresses that stays the same when traffic moves to the second Region within 60 seconds

constraint_reason: Service unavailable or not disposable in a personal same-day lab
